articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 103
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware campaigns, including the compromise of 4,000 legacy routers for proxy attacks, a VBScript-based WhatsApp distribution scheme, and a new loader for CASTLESTEALER. It provides a curated overview of ongoing global cyber threats and technical research.

articles.title: Anonymous-Linked Hacktivist Aubrey Cottle Jailed Over Texas GOP Cyberattack
articles.summary: Canadian hacktivist Aubrey Cottle has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for his role in a 2021 cyberattack targeting the Texas GOP website. The incident highlights the legal consequences for individuals involved in politically motivated hacking activities.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 583 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This Security Affairs newsletter highlights recent cybersecurity developments, including a new FBI warning regarding Russian intelligence exploiting Signal recovery keys and ongoing attacks against the hospitality sector.

articles.title: Data breach exposes up to 14.2 million email logins at six ISPs
articles.summary: Japanese telecommunications giant KDDI Corporation suffered a data breach impacting an email system shared by five other ISPs, resulting in the exposure of up to 14.2 million user credentials.

articles.title: Week in review: Fortibleed campaign’s impact on orgs, Cisco Unified CM flaw exploited
articles.summary: The weekly report highlights the impact of the Fortibleed campaign on organizations and details the exploitation of a vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager. It also discusses privacy limitations regarding encrypted DNS traffic.

articles.title: Ukraine Says Russian Intelligence Used Fake Support Texts to Steal Messaging Credentials
articles.summary: The SSU and FBI have exposed a coordinated Russian intelligence campaign using fraudulent support messages to compromise the accounts of government officials, military personnel, and activists globally. The operation aimed to gain unauthorized access to sensitive messaging credentials to facilitate espionage.

articles.title: New FBI Alert: Russian Intelligence Uses Signal Recovery Keys to Access Messages
articles.summary: The FBI and CISA have issued an updated advisory warning that Russian intelligence services are exploiting Signal Backup Recovery Keys to compromise user message history and gain unauthorized account access. This campaign represents a shift in strategy toward long-term surveillance through advanced phishing tactics.

articles.title: Hospitality Sector Hit by Phishing Campaign Using Fake Guest Complaint Emails
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified a long-running phishing campaign targeting the hospitality sector that deploys TonRAT malware using persistent techniques. The attacks, active since April 2026, specifically exploit guest communication channels to compromise organizational environments.

articles.title: Clean GitHub repo tricks AI coding agents into running malware
articles.summary: Malicious actors are embedding hidden payloads in GitHub repositories that exploit automated AI coding agents to execute malware during routine repository setup. This supply chain attack technique evades both traditional security scanners and human oversight.

articles.title: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Sol With Restricted Access and Stronger Cyber Safeguards
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a restricted preview of its GPT-5.6 model series, including the flagship model 'Sol,' as part of a collaborative initiative with the U.S. government to enhance cybersecurity safeguards.

articles.title: DirtyClone: Fourth Linux Kernel Flaw in Six Weeks Escalates to Root
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a critical Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw, dubbed DirtyClone, that allows attackers to rewrite memory executables without leaving disk traces. This vulnerability is the fourth in the DirtyFrag family and carries a high CVSS score of 8.8.

articles.title: It's looking like a hot, messy summer for security teams as AI finds countless previously hidden vulns
articles.summary: The integration of AI into vulnerability discovery is rapidly uncovering vast numbers of previously unknown security flaws, placing significant strain on cybersecurity teams. This surge in identified vulnerabilities is expected to create a challenging and resource-intensive summer for security operations.

articles.title: FBI: Russian hackers now target Signal backup recovery keys
articles.summary: Russian intelligence services are utilizing phishing campaigns to harvest Signal Backup Recovery Keys, enabling the decryption and unauthorized access of users' historical messages. This evolution in tactics poses a significant risk to the privacy of encrypted communications.

articles.title: 8 Top SAST Tools for Polyglot Monorepos and Platform Engineering in 2026
articles.summary: This article evaluates eight leading Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools optimized for handling complex, multi-language monorepos and large-scale platform engineering environments in 2026. It focuses on features like incremental scanning, automated ownership, and custom rule management.

articles.title: Even the Secret Service won't use company-issued phones
articles.summary: The U.S. Secret Service is facing scrutiny for security failures, including the use of personal cell phones for sensitive missions and a lack of threat detection capabilities on government-issued devices. These operational lapses highlight significant vulnerabilities in the agency's mobile security infrastructure.

articles.title: CISA sets urgent deadline to fix Cisco flaw exploited in attacks
articles.summary: CISA has issued an urgent directive requiring federal agencies to patch an actively exploited vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager Server by this Sunday. The mandate aims to mitigate risks posed by ongoing attacks targeting the flaw.

articles.title: FBI Warns Russian Intelligence Hackers Target Signal Backup Recovery Keys
articles.summary: The FBI and CISA have issued an alert regarding Russian intelligence actors who are phishing Signal users to obtain their backup recovery keys, enabling unauthorized access to message history and account takeovers.

articles.title: Woodgnat Hackers Use Mistic RAT to Broker Access for Ransomware Gangs
articles.summary: The Woodgnat hacking group is utilizing the Mistic RAT to compromise corporate networks, acting as initial access brokers for various ransomware syndicates. This operational model significantly increases the risk of downstream ransomware attacks for the victimized organizations.

articles.title: ATF cancels controversial commercial geolocation contract
articles.summary: The ATF has terminated a controversial geolocation tracking contract, citing that the pilot tool failed to meet agency needs despite congressional reports indicating it was utilized in hundreds of active investigations.

articles.title: New SharkLoader Malware Deploys Cobalt Strike in StrikeShark Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new malware family named SharkLoader, which is being utilized in the StrikeShark campaign to deploy Cobalt Strike Beacons against government and diplomatic targets. The attack highlights a sophisticated threat actor targeting specific geopolitical entities.

articles.title: Polymarket customers lose $3 million in supply-chain attack
articles.summary: Polymarket suffered a $3 million loss after a third-party vendor breach allowed attackers to inject a malicious script into the platform's frontend. The company has committed to fully reimbursing all affected customers.

articles.title: Cybersecurity firms targeted by fraudulent OpenAI organization invites
articles.summary: Threat actors are impersonating legitimate organizations through fraudulent OpenAI invites to harvest sensitive corporate information from employees. This social engineering campaign exploits trust in AI platforms to gain unauthorized access to internal data.

articles.title: Chinese APT CL-STA-1062 Expands Attacks on Southeast Asian Critical Infrastructure With Custom Malware
articles.summary: Chinese-speaking threat actor CL-STA-1062 is conducting persistent cyber espionage operations targeting critical infrastructure in Southeast Asia using custom malware and a new backdoor dubbed TinyRCT.

articles.title: Chinese-Speaking APT Deploys New TinyRCT Backdoor in Southeast Asia Campaign
articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking APT actor identified as CL-STA-1062 is targeting Southeast Asian government and energy entities using a new custom backdoor named TinyRCT. The campaign represents a focused effort against critical infrastructure in the region.

articles.title: Amazon Q flaw let booby-trapped Git repos execute code, swipe cloud creds
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in Amazon Q allowed attackers to execute malicious code and steal cloud credentials through booby-trapped Git repository configurations. This flaw highlights broader security concerns regarding the execution of commands by AI coding assistants.

articles.title: Your First GRC Agent: A Red Teamer's Walkthrough
articles.summary: This article explores the implementation of an AI-driven GRC agent designed to automate control monitoring, evidence gap identification, and remediation task management for compliance professionals.

articles.title: New Linux pedit COW Exploit Enables Root Access by Poisoning Cached Binaries
articles.summary: A critical local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem allows unprivileged users to gain root access via an out-of-bounds write. A public exploit for this flaw, dubbed 'pedit COW,' is already available, posing an immediate risk to affected systems.

articles.title: Amazon Q Developer Flaw Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code via MCP Configs
articles.summary: A high-severity vulnerability in Amazon Q Developer allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code and steal cloud credentials by exploiting the application's handling of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Amazon has since released a patch to address the security flaw.

articles.title: Russia accuses Apple of ‘political censorship’ after VK apps removed from App Store
articles.summary: Apple removed several major Russian applications, including VKontakte, from its App Store, prompting accusations of political censorship from the Russian government.

articles.title: Turla group adds more malware to Russia’s espionage efforts against Ukraine
articles.summary: Google researchers have identified a new piece of malware called StockStay, which is being utilized by the Russian threat actor group Turla in its ongoing espionage campaigns against Ukraine.

articles.title: Russia used social engineering to breach prominent messaging accounts, Ukraine says
articles.summary: The Ukrainian Security Service reported that Russian operatives successfully compromised high-profile messaging accounts by masquerading as technical support staff to steal user credentials. The campaign relied on social engineering tactics rather than software exploits to gain unauthorized access.

articles.title: macOS Flaw Allowed Standard Users to Disable CrowdStrike and Kandji Security Tools
articles.summary: A macOS XPC vulnerability allowed unprivileged users to disable security software like CrowdStrike and Kandji. The vendors have since released patches to address the issue discovered by XM Cyber.

articles.title: CISA Adds Exploited PTC Windchill RCE Flaw to KEV as Web Shell Attacks Continue
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in PTC Windchill software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to ongoing active exploitation. The flaw is being leveraged by attackers to deploy web shells.

articles.title: Miasma campaign poisons 20-plus npm packages, hunts for developer secrets
articles.summary: The Miasma supply chain attack has compromised over 20 npm packages, including Leo Platform and RStreams, to steal developer credentials and target software maintainers. Microsoft has identified the campaign, which focuses on harvesting secrets through malicious package injections.

articles.title: FCC votes to toughen rules in bid to better protect undersea cables
articles.summary: The FCC has approved stricter regulations for undersea cable infrastructure, including a new requirement for submarine line terminal equipment operators to obtain licenses. This initiative aims to strengthen the security and oversight of critical telecommunications infrastructure.

articles.title: Proof’s x401 establishes an open protocol for AI agent identity and authorization
articles.summary: Proof has introduced x401, an open and issuer-neutral protocol designed to verify the identity and authorization of AI agents interacting with websites and APIs. The framework allows services to validate agent claims, such as organizational affiliation or signing authority, to ensure secure and trusted AI interactions.

articles.title: New DirtyClone Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Local Users Gain Root via Cloned Packets
articles.summary: The DirtyClone Linux kernel vulnerability allows local attackers to achieve root-level privilege escalation by corrupting file-backed memory through cloned network packets. Identified as CVE-2026-43503, the flaw has a CVSS score of 8.8 and is part of the DirtyFrag family.

articles.title: Critical open-source projects get a new security framework
articles.summary: The Linux Foundation has launched Akrites, a new industry initiative designed to streamline the remediation and disclosure process for vulnerabilities in critical open-source software. This framework addresses the increased risk posed by AI-accelerated exploitation timelines.

articles.title: Guardian Agents: The Next Layer of Identity Governance
articles.summary: The rapid integration of autonomous AI agents in enterprise environments is creating significant security gaps, as traditional identity governance frameworks are ill-equipped to manage machine-speed access. The headline highlights the urgent need for new governance structures to oversee these non-human actors.

articles.title: Activist Phone Hacked With Cellebrite After Russia Contract Cancellation
articles.summary: Russian authorities utilized Cellebrite forensic tools to bypass security measures on an activist's confiscated iPhone 12, despite the company's prior public commitment to terminate contracts with the country. This incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding the potential for forensic software misuse against political targets.

articles.title: Miasma Malware Targets npm Packages and GitHub Actions in Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: The Miasma malware family has expanded its supply chain attack campaign to compromise additional npm packages and GitHub Actions, while also extending its reach into the Go ecosystem.

articles.title: Synology issues critical fix for MailPlus Server vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Synology has released a critical security update for its MailPlus Server to address three vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to conduct unauthorized file operations, access internal services, and trigger denial-of-service attacks. Users are advised to apply the patch immediately to secure their private email infrastructure.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Cisco and PTC Windchill and FlexPLM flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include critical flaws affecting Cisco, PTC Windchill, and FlexPLM products. Organizations are urged to address these vulnerabilities to mitigate the risk of exploitation.

articles.title: Ransomware gangs find Europe’s weakest link in third-party suppliers
articles.summary: A 2026 report by Black Kite reveals that ransomware attacks against European organizations are rising, with threat actors increasingly targeting supply chains as their primary entry point. The study highlights the convergence of rising ransomware activity, vulnerable third-party suppliers, and complex regulatory landscapes.

articles.title: A decade of infrastructure development, one new name: Coinspaid Dev
articles.summary: The team behind Coinspaid Solutions has rebranded as Coinspaid Dev to focus on positioning themselves as a prominent voice in blockchain infrastructure engineering.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of Photo ZIP Phishing Campaign Targeting Hotels with Node.js Implant
articles.summary: Microsoft is tracking an ongoing phishing campaign targeting hospitality organizations across Europe and Asia that uses malicious ZIP files to deploy a Node.js implant. The threat actors remain unidentified, and their ultimate objectives for compromising front-desk systems are currently unknown.

articles.title: Mirage2FA phishing kit uses HTML smuggling to steal Microsoft 365 credentials
articles.summary: Fortra researchers have identified Mirage2FA, a sophisticated phishing kit that uses HTML smuggling and obfuscated JavaScript to bypass security filters and steal Microsoft 365 credentials during MFA processes. The campaign utilizes business-themed lures like fake invoices and payment requests to target users via email.

articles.title: Mystery hackers use novel SharkLoader dropper against governments, software devs
articles.summary: Kaspersky researchers have identified a global cyberattack campaign dubbed StrikeShark, which uses a new, previously unknown dropper called SharkLoader to target government and software development organizations. The sophisticated operation was uncovered during the investigation of a targeted attack on a diplomatic entity in Indonesia.

articles.title: Russia Used Cellebrite on Jailed Activist's iPhone Months After Sales Cutoff
articles.summary: Russian authorities successfully accessed an activist's iPhone using Cellebrite forensic tools months after the company officially ceased operations in Russia. The evidence, documented by Citizen Lab, highlights potential lapses in export compliance or the use of legacy hardware.

articles.title: Third-Party Breach at Polymarket Leads to $2.94M Crypto Theft
articles.summary: Polymarket experienced a security breach after attackers compromised a third-party vendor to inject malicious code into its website, resulting in the theft of $2.94 million in user funds.

articles.title: SIM-swapping gang busted in international police operation
articles.summary: Polish authorities, in collaboration with the FBI and HSI, dismantled an international cybercrime gang responsible for SIM-swapping attacks, cryptocurrency theft, and money laundering. Four suspects were arrested as part of an ongoing investigation into the group's organized cyber operations.

articles.title: ZeroTier Quantum RC2 brings post-quantum security closer to general availability
articles.summary: ZeroTier has released the second release candidate for its quantum-secure networking platform, aligning with upcoming U.S. government post-quantum cryptography standards. This move aims to protect network traffic against future threats posed by advanced quantum computing.

articles.title: ThreatModeler introduces Nexus to automate threat modeling with AI governance
articles.summary: ThreatModeler has launched Nexus, an agentic threat modeling platform that leverages AI governance to automate security architecture analysis throughout the software development lifecycle.

articles.title: macOS.Gaslight: North Korea-Linked Malware That Tries to Gaslight the Analyst
articles.summary: North Korean threat actors have developed a Rust-based macOS implant called macOS.Gaslight that utilizes prompt injection payloads to deceive AI-driven security analysis tools. The malware was discovered after an Apple XProtect update and represents a novel tactic in anti-forensic techniques.

articles.title: Google Details Turla's New STOCKSTAY Backdoor Used in Ukraine Espionage Attacks
articles.summary: Google Threat Intelligence has identified a new .NET backdoor named STOCKSTAY, developed by the Russian-linked threat actor Turla for use in espionage operations against Ukrainian government and military entities. The malware is part of an ongoing campaign targeting organizations with interests in Italian foreign policy.

articles.title: Microsoft gives Windows 10 users an unexpected extra year of free security updates
articles.summary: Microsoft has extended the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10 consumers by an additional year, providing security coverage until October 12, 2027. This update allows users to maintain device security longer than previously anticipated without immediate forced upgrades.

articles.title: Security boss thought MFA would be too much security
articles.summary: A security executive chose to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) protocols for leadership, citing concerns over excessive security despite enforcing them for the rest of the workforce. This decision highlights a hypocritical 'rules for thee, not for me' approach that undermines organizational security posture.

articles.title: A privacy-first take on local malware analysis
articles.summary: The article discusses the privacy risks of uploading suspicious files to public malware repositories, where attackers can track the distribution of their own tools. It advocates for local malware analysis techniques to maintain operational security.

articles.title: New infosec products of the month: June 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights several new cybersecurity product releases for June 2026, including Asimily's new Segmentation Orchestration tool for automated device risk management. It provides a roundup of updates from various vendors aimed at enhancing security operations and asset visibility.

articles.title: Chinese cybersecurity company claims it’s built a better-than-Mythos bug finder
articles.summary: Qihoo 360, a Chinese cybersecurity firm restricted by the US, claims to have developed an automated vulnerability discovery tool that surpasses Mythos, positioning it as a countermeasure against AI-driven cyber weaponization.

articles.title: Anthropic is testing desktop-like Claude Cowork for mobile
articles.summary: Anthropic is testing a 'Claude Cowork' feature for mobile devices, enabling users to manage long-running AI tasks directly from their phones. This expansion increases the accessibility and mobile integration of their AI agent capabilities.

articles.title: Poland busts SIM-swapping gang tied to millions in crypto theft
articles.summary: Polish authorities have arrested four individuals involved in a cybercrime group that utilized SIM-swapping and email hijacking to steal millions in cryptocurrency. The operation focused on compromising telecommunications partners to facilitate these fraudulent attacks.

articles.title: Self-destructing Mistic backdoor linked to access broker selling corporate footholds to ransomware gangs
articles.summary: A self-destructing backdoor named Mistic is being used by an access broker to compromise organizations in the insurance, education, IT, and professional services sectors for later resale to ransomware groups.

articles.title: CL-STA-1062 Targets Southeast Asian Governments and Critical Infrastructure
articles.summary: The threat actor group CL-STA-1062 is conducting espionage operations against Southeast Asian government agencies and critical infrastructure using a hybrid toolkit featuring the custom TinyRCT backdoor.

articles.title: Tata Electronics Confirms Data Breach After 630GB Leak Claim Targets Apple and Tesla
articles.summary: Tata Electronics has confirmed a significant data breach involving 630GB of stolen information, including sensitive documents related to its supply chain partnerships with Apple and Tesla. The incident follows claims made on a hacker forum regarding unauthorized access to the company's IT systems.

articles.title: Ex-Huntress analyst claims company insider fed info to a ransomware crim. Social media drama ensues
articles.summary: A former Huntress analyst has publicly alleged that an internal employee leaked sensitive information to ransomware actors, further claiming the company prioritized its impending IPO over addressing security concerns. The accusations have sparked significant controversy on social media, raising questions about internal security protocols.

articles.title: FCC passes new cybersecurity rules for emergency systems, undersea cables
articles.summary: The FCC has approved updated cybersecurity regulations aimed at securing national emergency communication systems against hijacking and strengthening security review requirements for undersea cable providers.

articles.title: Order-tracking app Shop abused to push callback phishing attacks
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting the Shopify Shop order-tracking app by injecting fake purchase receipts into user histories to conduct callback phishing attacks. These campaigns aim to deceive users into disclosing sensitive information or installing malicious remote access software.

articles.title: Curl Fixes a 25-Year-Old Bug in Its Largest CVE Release Yet
articles.summary: The Curl project released a significant update addressing 18 vulnerabilities in libcurl, including a critical memory safety bug that has persisted for 25 years. The patch covers a range of security flaws, including authentication bypass and host validation issues.

articles.title: DHS chief says president has met with potential CISA nominee; agency plans to hire 600
articles.summary: The Department of Homeland Security is preparing to fill the vacant CISA director position and subsequently expand the agency's workforce by 600 employees. The White House is currently evaluating potential candidates to lead the agency.

articles.title: Microsoft quietly extends free Windows 10 ESU support to October 2027
articles.summary: Microsoft has extended its free Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10 consumers by one year, now providing security support until October 12, 2027.

articles.title: Fake GTA 6 Early Access Websites Target Gamers with Malware and Crypto Scams
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are exploiting high anticipation for GTA 6 by creating fraudulent websites that deliver malware and solicit cryptocurrency payments under the guise of early access. These campaigns primarily target PC and Android users through deceptive promotional tactics.

articles.title: New macOS malware embeds fake errors to confuse AI analysis tools
articles.summary: A new macOS malware named Gaslight employs prompt injection techniques and fake debugging data to deliberately deceive AI-based security analysis tools. This strategy aims to evade detection by causing confusion during the automated malware inspection process.

articles.title: Federal court rules Trump election-focused executive order illegal
articles.summary: A federal court has struck down an executive order that mandated the creation of federal voter lists and restricted USPS mail ballot operations, ruling the provisions unconstitutional.

articles.title: PirloTV sports piracy network disrupted as 44 domains seized
articles.summary: Authorities have disrupted the PirloTV sports piracy network by seizing 44 domains linked to the illegal streaming operation.

articles.title: Upwind Security Brings AI Visibility to the Endpoint, Unifying Cloud and Device Security
articles.summary: Upwind Security has launched an AI-powered sensor that integrates endpoint activity with cloud security data to improve visibility into AI-related risks and developer activities. The platform aims to unify security monitoring across both cloud environments and endpoint devices.

articles.title: Inside Mistic, the New Stealth Backdoor in Ransomware Intrusions
articles.summary: Mistic is a new, stealthy backdoor utilized by KongTuke-linked threat actors to maintain persistent access in ransomware attacks across various industries. The malware is designed for long-term infiltration while minimizing noise to avoid detection.

articles.title: Bluekit phishing kit adopts browser-in-the-middle for login theft
articles.summary: The Bluekit phishing-as-a-service platform has expanded its infrastructure and integrated browser-in-the-middle techniques to enhance credential theft capabilities. This evolution highlights a growing trend in sophisticated automated phishing operations targeting user logins.

articles.title: Russia uses Cellebrite to break into human rights activist’s phone, even after cancellation of contract
articles.summary: Reports indicate that Russian authorities continued to use Cellebrite forensic technology to access the phone of activist Andrey Pivovarov despite the company's publicly announced termination of its contract with the country.

articles.title: Another Russian dairy company reportedly disrupted by cyberattack
articles.summary: A dairy manufacturer in Russia's Bashkortostan region has experienced operational disruptions following a cyberattack, marking another incident targeting the country's dairy sector.

articles.title: Minnesota man known as ‘Snoopy’ sentenced in DraftKings hack
articles.summary: Nathan Austad, also known as 'Snoopy,' has been sentenced as the final defendant involved in the 2022 unauthorized access breach of DraftKings accounts. He was convicted for operating a criminal storefront that sold access to compromised user accounts.

articles.title: Chrome Ad Blocker with 10M+ Installs Found with Dormant Script Injection Capability
articles.summary: A popular Chrome extension with over 10 million installs, 'Adblock for YouTube', was found to contain a dormant script injection capability that allows for arbitrary JavaScript execution. The extension, which carried a Google-verified 'Featured' badge, poses a significant supply chain risk to its large user base.

articles.title: Stealthy new backdoor surfaces in attacks on multiple sectors
articles.summary: A new backdoor named Mistic, linked to the financially motivated threat actor Woodgnat, is being deployed in targeted attacks against the insurance, education, IT, and professional services sectors. This threat actor is known for facilitating initial access for various prominent ransomware operations.

articles.title: The Four Elevations of Effective Fraud Prevention
articles.summary: The article outlines a multi-layered approach to fraud prevention, emphasizing that organizations must monitor entire ecosystems rather than isolated transactions to effectively counter modern threats. By increasing visibility across accounts and platforms, businesses can significantly improve their overall fraud detection capabilities.

articles.title: Checksum API Agent generates and maintains stateful API tests
articles.summary: Checksum has released an API Agent designed to automatically generate and maintain stateful, journey-based tests for backend APIs to ensure testing keeps pace with rapid code development. The tool integrates into existing pipelines to address testing coverage gaps created by AI-accelerated endpoint generation.

articles.title: Reco Agent Security helps organizations govern AI agents and reduce exposure
articles.summary: Reco has launched Reco Agent Security to help organizations manage the risks of autonomous AI agents, including data exposure and unauthorized process disruption across enterprise ecosystems. The platform provides governance and monitoring capabilities to secure AI-driven workflows and interconnected applications.

articles.title: Mitiga unveils Agentic Runtime Security for cloud, SaaS, identity, and AI protection
articles.summary: Mitiga has launched Agentic Runtime Security, a platform designed to provide automated detection and response across cloud, SaaS, identity, and AI environments. The solution aims to shift security focus from endpoint-centric models toward protecting the modern, third-party-dependent digital infrastructure.

articles.title: ControlMonkey connects backup visibility with cloud recovery readiness
articles.summary: ControlMonkey has introduced Data Backup Correlation to its Cyber Resilience Platform, enabling organizations to gain visibility into backup coverage and recovery readiness for AWS and Azure environments. This new capability helps cloud teams identify recoverable data assets and bridge the gap between backup posture and cloud configuration.

articles.title: Veritone introduces Assess to streamline evidence analysis and compliance reviews
articles.summary: Veritone has launched Veritone Assess, an AI-powered tool designed to help public sector agencies streamline evidence analysis and automate compliance reviews for complex datasets. The platform identifies intelligence gaps and policy inconsistencies to improve the speed and accuracy of investigative decision-making.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Smart TV Proxyware, 24-Year curl Bug, AI Crime Forums + 13 More Stories
articles.summary: This bulletin covers a diverse range of cybersecurity issues, including smart TV proxyware, a long-standing curl vulnerability, and the rise of AI-driven cybercrime forums. The report highlights how mundane operational failures and legacy security gaps continue to be the primary drivers of current threats.

articles.title: runZero 5.0 unifies exposure management to accelerate risk reduction
articles.summary: runZero has launched version 5.0 of its platform, which integrates asset discovery, vulnerability management, and remediation workflows to help organizations proactively reduce their attack surface. The update aims to address the challenges of siloed security data by unifying the exposure management lifecycle.

articles.title: Ukraine's state postal operator reports app disruption after cyberattack
articles.summary: Ukraine's state postal operator, Ukrposhta, is experiencing service disruptions within its mobile application following a suspected cyberattack. The entity has not identified the perpetrator or the specific nature of the attack.

articles.title: Russia used Cellebrite phone-hacking tool to crack down on dissident after firm cut off country
articles.summary: Despite publicly pledging to cease operations in Russia in 2021, Cellebrite's forensic software was reportedly still being utilized by Russian authorities to target dissidents, highlighting challenges in controlling the proliferation of dual-use surveillance technology.

articles.title: Webinar: Why account takeovers remain one of the hardest threats to stop
articles.summary: This webinar discusses why account takeover attacks are difficult to mitigate due to the abuse of legitimate credentials and explores how behavioral AI can improve detection and response. The session focuses on leveraging automation to secure trusted services against unauthorized access.

articles.title: Suspected Cyberattack Sends Fake Emergency Alert to Phones Across Brazil
articles.summary: Brazil's national emergency alert system was suspended following a suspected cyberattack that triggered false notifications across the country. Authorities are currently investigating the incident to determine the nature of the breach.

articles.title: Surviving the Mythos Era: Richard Bejtlich on the Case for NDR
articles.summary: Richard Bejtlich argues that security teams must look beyond standard alerts and leverage Network Detection and Response (NDR) to gain the necessary context for effective incident investigation.

articles.title: Seemplicity AI Analysts focus remediation on exploitable risks
articles.summary: Seemplicity has introduced AI Analysts, autonomous agents designed to automate vulnerability triage and focus remediation efforts on verified, exploitable risks. The solution addresses the challenge of rapidly shortening exploit windows by replacing manual processes with evidence-based investigation workflows.

articles.title: New Gaslight macOS Malware Uses Prompt Injection to Disrupt AI-Assisted Analysis
articles.summary: The newly discovered Gaslight macOS malware leverages prompt injection techniques to manipulate AI-powered analysis tools into ignoring or misinterpreting its malicious payload. This tactic represents an emerging trend of adversarial attacks specifically targeting AI-assisted cybersecurity workflows.

articles.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Zero-Day CVE-2026-20245 Exploited Months Before Disclosure
articles.summary: An unknown threat actor exploited a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-20245, for at least two months prior to its public disclosure, allowing for privileged command execution. The flaw, which holds a CVSS score of 7.8, highlights a significant lag between active exploitation and vendor patching.

articles.title: Entrust uses biometrics to verify users during high-risk transactions
articles.summary: Entrust has launched a biometric authentication solution designed to prevent account takeovers by verifying the user's identity during high-risk activities such as account recovery and large transactions. This approach shifts authentication from simple login verification to continuous, identity-centric assurance.

articles.title: YesWeHack automates penetration testing with AI-powered agents
articles.summary: YesWeHack has launched 'Agentic Pentest,' an AI-powered solution that utilizes autonomous agents to provide on-demand penetration testing and rapid vulnerability identification. The tool supports multiple testing methodologies across various digital assets to help organizations assess real-world exploitability.

articles.title: Why patch directives only go so far
articles.summary: This article highlights that patch directives are insufficient for organizations that have already experienced a breach, specifically noting a six-week window of undetected access via a compromised VPN. It emphasizes that patching alone cannot remediate an environment where attackers have already established persistence.

articles.title: Forescout brings PQC visibility to IT, OT, IoT, and IoMT environments
articles.summary: Forescout has launched new PQC Readiness and Encryption Hygiene Dashboards to help organizations identify and manage quantum computing risks across IT, OT, IoT, and IoMT environments. This tool assists businesses in meeting regulatory and board-level demands for post-quantum cryptographic awareness.

articles.title: New Mistic Backdoor Linked to KongTuke in ClickFix and ModeloRAT Campaigns
articles.summary: A new stealthy backdoor called Mistic, also known as MLTBackdoor, is being utilized by initial access brokers in financially motivated attacks against various sectors including education and IT. The threat is linked to KongTuke and is active in ongoing ClickFix and ModeloRAT campaigns.

articles.title: WhatsApp will warn users before they message a potential scammer
articles.summary: WhatsApp is introducing a warning screen for chats with unfamiliar phone numbers to help users identify and avoid potential scammers. This feature automatically assesses the trustworthiness of numbers before allowing users to initiate conversations.

articles.title: Stellar Cyber improves threat detection and data onboarding in new updates
articles.summary: Stellar Cyber has updated its security platform to versions 6.5 and 6.6, introducing AI-driven workflows, enhanced threat detection, and improved data onboarding capabilities. These updates aim to streamline security operations for MSSPs and enterprise teams by reducing alert fatigue and increasing investigative context.

articles.title: Bitdefender RealCheck analyzes videos for deepfakes and fraud
articles.summary: Bitdefender has introduced RealCheck, a consumer-facing tool designed to detect deepfakes and identify malicious intent in video content. The solution aims to combat rising threats like financial fraud, credential theft, and defamation.

articles.title: Nathan Austad Pleads Guilty in DraftKings Hacking Scheme, Gets 18 Months
articles.summary: Nathan Austad has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for his role in a 2022 credential-stuffing attack on DraftKings that compromised 1,600 accounts and resulted in the theft of $600,000.

articles.title: UK school’s network left wide open for invasion, student found
articles.summary: A UK school suffered a significant security oversight when a student discovered the network's administrative password stored in plain text within an Active Directory description field. This improper configuration exposed the entire school network to potential unauthorized access and exploitation.

articles.summary: Mandiant discovered that a high-severity zero-day vulnerability in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, tracked as CVE-2026-20245, was exploited by a threat actor to achieve root access months before public disclosure. The flaw enables an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands with elevated privileges.

articles.title: Nation-state actors cracked critical Australian infrastructure to ‘cripple it at a time of their choosing’
articles.summary: Nation-state actors successfully infiltrated critical Australian infrastructure to establish the capability for future sabotage. Australian intelligence agencies disrupted the operation by coordinating with international counterparts to expose the threat.

articles.title: Google releases new privacy controls for activity history, personalization
articles.summary: Google has introduced updated privacy settings for Search and Google Play, allowing users to better manage their activity history and personalized recommendations. This update aims to provide individuals with more granular control over how their data is stored and utilized for personalization.

articles.title: The hits keep on coming for Cisco vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Cisco is currently managing an actively exploited vulnerability, CVE-2026-20230, alongside new findings that indicate a previous SD-WAN zero-day is more severe than initially assessed.

articles.title: DraftKings hacker 'Snoopy' sentenced to 18 months in prison

articles.summary: Mandiant discovered that attackers exploited a Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN zero-day vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20245, to establish unauthorized root access on compromised devices. This revelation provides critical insight into the methods used to gain deep persistence within network infrastructure.

articles.summary: A malicious Microsoft Edge extension named 'Edgecution' exploits the browser's Native Messaging feature to bypass sandbox protections and deliver a Python-based ransomware payload. This technique demonstrates a critical bridge between browser-based extensions and host-level execution.

articles.title: Operation Endgame Disrupts StealC, Amadey and SocGholish Malware Networks
articles.summary: Operation Endgame successfully dismantled critical infrastructure for major malware families, including StealC, Amadey, and SocGholish, leading to the seizure of millions of stolen credentials. articles.summary: Microsoft and international law enforcement agencies collaborated to disrupt the infrastructure of three cybercrime-as-a-service operations. The initiative targeted over 300 servers, aiming to dismantle the underlying supply chain of malware distribution.

articles.title: Malicious hackers exploit Cisco zero-day for highest access level at communications service provider
articles.summary: Mandiant identified that malicious actors exploited a Cisco zero-day vulnerability to obtain root-level access within a communications service provider's network. The full extent of the intrusion and the identity of the attackers remain under investigation.

articles.title: Europol Disrupts StealC and Amadey Malware Infrastructure in Operation Endgame
articles.summary: Europol led a multi-national law enforcement operation, titled 'Operation Endgame', to successfully dismantle the command-and-control infrastructure of the widespread StealC and Amadey malware families.

articles.title: Microsoft uses AI to link two malware operations in racketeering suit
articles.summary: Microsoft leveraged AI to identify and connect the StealC and Amadey malware operations, leading to a legal action that resulted in the shutdown of over 200 command-and-control servers.

articles.title: CISA Warns Critical Lantronix EDS5000 Flaw Is Being Actively Exploited
articles.summary: CISA has issued an alert regarding the active exploitation of a critical code injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-67038) in Lantronix EDS5000 Series devices. Federal agencies are mandated to implement security patches by June 26, 2026.

articles.title: Amadey and StealC Malware Network Disrupted, 27M Stolen Credentials Recovered
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies and private tech partners collaborated to dismantle the command-and-control infrastructure of the Amadey and StealC botnets, successfully recovering 27 million stolen credentials. This operation aimed to cripple the distribution networks used for ransomware, fraud, and attacks on critical infrastructure.

articles.title: New GhostShell Hacking Group Targets Ukraine’s Drone Defense Sector
articles.summary: The GhostShell hacking group is conducting a cyber espionage campaign against Ukraine's drone defense sector by distributing malicious files disguised as official drone documentation to exfiltrate sensitive credentials. The attack leverages social engineering tactics to compromise defense personnel and gain access to classified information.

articles.title: Law enforcement hits StealC and Amadey malware networks
articles.summary: International law enforcement, supported by private sector partners, successfully dismantled the infrastructure for the StealC and Amadey malware networks. This operation targeted the delivery mechanisms used by these criminal groups to harvest sensitive data.

articles.title: CISA warns of max severity Ubiquiti flaws exploited in attacks
articles.summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding active exploitation of critical vulnerabilities in Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix serial-to-ethernet devices. Users are advised to patch these flaws immediately to prevent potential unauthorized access.

articles.title: Amadey, StealC malware operations disrupted in Operation Endgame action
articles.summary: Microsoft and international law enforcement agencies have successfully disrupted the infrastructure supporting the Amadey and StealC malware operations under the multi-national Operation Endgame initiative.

articles.title: German rail services resume after wireless communications outage
articles.summary: Deutsche Bahn experienced a nationwide railway service disruption caused by a technical malfunction in its 2G-based GSM-R communications infrastructure. Operations have since resumed following the resolution of the outage.

articles.title: Algerian national accused of running cybercrime marketplaces extradited to US
articles.summary: An Algerian national allegedly operating online marketplaces for cybercrime tools has been extradited from Spain to the United States to face charges of bank fraud conspiracy.

articles.title: Securing the service desk: Why social engineering attacks keep succeeding
articles.summary: Service desks are increasingly targeted by attackers using social engineering to gain unauthorized access through password resets and MFA bypasses. The article outlines these tactics and provides defensive strategies for organizations to mitigate these risks.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Claude Tag gives AI agents independent identities
articles.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Tag, a feature that assigns AI agents independent identities and specific tool access permissions within shared workspaces. This architecture isolates AI activity from individual user credentials, effectively reducing the risk of unauthorized data exposure in team environments.

articles.title: Why Frontier AI makes prioritization the most important part of your CTEM program
articles.summary: The rapid emergence of frontier AI is expected to cause a massive surge in vulnerability disclosures, necessitating a transition toward Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) for effective risk prioritization. Traditional vulnerability management programs are deemed inadequate to handle the accelerating volume of threats.

articles.title: Fake npm Packages Impersonate PostCSS Tool to Steal Chrome Passwords
articles.summary: Malicious npm packages disguised as the PostCSS tool are infecting Windows systems with remote access trojans to exfiltrate stored Chrome browser passwords. The campaign utilizes a staged infection process to stealthily deploy malware onto developer environments.

articles.title: Indian auto giant Bajaj Auto hit by ransomware incident
articles.summary: Indian automotive manufacturer Bajaj Auto confirmed a ransomware attack, prompting the company to implement containment measures to mitigate the incident's impact. The breach was reported via a regulatory filing shortly after its detection.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM Flaw CVE-2026-20230 Actively Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager is currently being exploited in the wild via CVE-2026-20230, a high-severity vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to achieve root access through SSRF and arbitrary file writes.

articles.title: Cordyceps CI/CD Flaws Expose 300+ GitHub Repositories to Supply-Chain Attacks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a critical CI/CD workflow vulnerability dubbed 'Cordyceps' that exposes over 300 GitHub repositories to potential supply-chain attacks. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to hijack workflows and gain full control over major organizational repositories.

articles.title: In a first, a court takedown goes after two cybercrime tools at once
articles.summary: Microsoft and its partners successfully disrupted over 200 command and control servers associated with the Amadey and StealC malware, marking the first time two cybercrime tools were taken down simultaneously via a court order.

articles.title: Phishing attack on healthcare firm Xsolis impacts 1.4 million people
articles.summary: Healthcare technology firm Xsolis confirmed that a targeted phishing attack led to unauthorized network access, affecting approximately 1.4 million individuals. The incident, which occurred in January 2026, compromised sensitive data managed by the company's AI-powered healthcare software.

articles.title: SuperOps and Guardz bundle IT operations and security into one product for MSPs
articles.summary: SuperOps and Guardz have formed a partnership to offer a unified platform for MSPs that combines IT operations, remote monitoring, and AI-driven security capabilities. This integration aims to streamline workflows by merging operational and security data into a single, bundled solution.

articles.title: London cops bring live facial recognition to West End
articles.summary: London police have implemented live facial recognition technology in the West End, drawing criticism from privacy advocates who argue it violates the principle of policing by consent.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM flaw actively exploited to drop webshells (CVE-2026-20230)
articles.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager is currently being exploited in the wild via a Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability (CVE-2026-20230) to deploy webshells and achieve remote code execution. Attackers are utilizing automated sweeps originating from Tor to target the WebDialer component and establish persistence.

articles.title: Dawn of the Apex Agentic Adversary
articles.summary: The shift toward autonomous agentic threats is ending the era of human-speed cybersecurity, necessitating a transition to real-time, automated defense mechanisms. This evolution renders traditional manual patch cycles and response timelines dangerously obsolete.

articles.title: Stealthy Mistic backdoor linked to ransomware access broker KongTuke
articles.summary: A newly discovered backdoor called Mistic is being utilized by the threat actor KongTuke to facilitate ransomware attacks against organizations in the insurance, education, and IT sectors.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix EDS5000 plugin flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added critical vulnerabilities affecting Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix EDS5000 devices to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to active exploitation. This mandate requires U.S. federal agencies to address these security gaps within a specified timeframe to mitigate ongoing risks.

articles.title: LastPass customer data exposed through Klue supply chain attack
articles.summary: LastPass customer data was exposed after attackers leveraged OAuth tokens compromised during a supply chain attack on the third-party platform Klue. The breach allowed unauthorized access to LastPass's Salesforce environment through integrated systems.

articles.title: FortiBleed: The Broker Who Turned 73,000 Firewalls Into a Product Catalog
articles.summary: A researcher discovered a publicly exposed server containing valid login credentials for over 73,000 Fortinet firewalls, highlighting a significant access-brokering operation. This data leak, dubbed FortiBleed, compromises the security of thousands of global organizations.

articles.title: Google Workspace expands password reset alerts to all admins
articles.summary: Google is expanding its Workspace alert system to notify administrators whenever any administrative account password is reset, enhancing visibility and security for privileged accounts. This update helps organizations more effectively monitor and respond to potential unauthorized access attempts.

articles.title: Open-source security is posing challenges governments can’t easily solve
articles.summary: The widespread and decentralized nature of open-source software, combined with insufficient corporate oversight and emerging AI threats, is creating complex security challenges that current government strategies struggle to address.

articles.title: DoJ Seizes Huione Cloud Account Tied to Cyber Scam Money Laundering
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice seized a cloud computing account used by Cambodia-based Huione Group subsidiaries for laundering cyber scam proceeds. This action coincided with new U.S. Treasury sanctions targeting entities linked to the Prince Group for their role in illicit financial activities.

articles.title: One Railway Radio Outage Stopped Trains Across Germany and Nobody Knew Why
articles.summary: A nationwide GSM-R network failure in Germany forced Deutsche Bahn to halt all train operations across the country. The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities and reliability issues within aging railway communications infrastructure.

articles.title: Best Crypto Payment Solutions for E-Commerce Businesses
articles.summary: This article provides a comparative overview of cryptocurrency payment gateways and tools designed to facilitate digital currency transactions for e-commerce platforms. It focuses on the functional features of financial technology integration rather than specific security threats.

articles.title: Qodo expands platform to help teams govern AI-generated code and engineering standards
articles.summary: Qodo has introduced three new governance capabilities—Cross-Repo Code Review, Custom Rules Miner, and Skill Review Standards—to help enterprises manage the security and quality of AI-generated code. These tools aim to mitigate risks associated with the increasing autonomy of AI agents in the software development lifecycle.

articles.title: Brinqa BYOAI lets organizations use any AI platform with trusted risk data
articles.summary: Brinqa has introduced a 'Bring Your Own AI' (BYOAI) capability that allows enterprises to integrate various AI models and agents with its exposure intelligence platform. This integration ensures that AI-driven risk analysis is based on consistent, accurate, and up-to-date security data.

articles.title: Cequence introduces behavioral bot detection and biometric verification without CAPTCHAs
articles.summary: Cequence Security has launched Intent Graph and Biometric Check to provide bot defense across web, mobile, and AI traffic, eliminating the need for traditional CAPTCHAs. These new capabilities utilize behavioral architecture to detect sophisticated bots that typically bypass standard client-side signals.

articles.title: New Secure Code Warrior framework helps CISOs govern AI-driven software development
articles.summary: Secure Code Warrior has launched the SCW AI Adoption Model, a framework designed to help CISOs manage and govern the integration of AI in software development as it scales toward autonomous agentic systems. It provides guidance on necessary training and security controls based on an organization's specific level of AI adoption.

articles.title: DigiCert brings independent trust validation to confidential computing environments
articles.summary: DigiCert has partnered with Google Cloud to provide independent PKI-based cryptographic verification for confidential computing environments. This initiative aims to ensure the authenticity and integrity of sensitive cloud-hosted workloads and infrastructure.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM Flaw Exploited After PoC Reveals File-Write Path to Root
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical improper input validation vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, designated as CVE-2026-20230, which allows for remote, unauthenticated file-write access to the root directory.

articles.title: Where IT meets OT and railway cybersecurity gets harder
articles.summary: This interview explores the cybersecurity challenges of integrating legacy operational technology with modern IT in railway systems, focusing on increased attack surfaces, regulatory compliance, and risk management. It discusses how technical teams handle patching vulnerabilities while maintaining critical service availability and addressing liability concerns.

articles.title: You have got to be KDDI-ng – Japanese telco exposes 14.2 million managed email credentials
articles.summary: Japanese telecommunications company KDDI suffered a massive data breach, exposing the managed email credentials of 14.2 million users across five different ISPs. The incident highlights significant security gaps in the management of user account information.

articles.title: Samsung KNOX Kernel UAF Exposes Millions of Galaxy Devices
articles.summary: A kernel use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-20971) within Samsung's KNOX security stack allowed potential exploitation through memory corruption, affecting millions of Galaxy devices before a patch was released in January 2026.

articles.title: OpenClaw’s Skill Marketplace and the Emerging AI Supply Chain Threat
articles.summary: Unit 42 researchers identified that the ClawHub marketplace hosts malicious AI skills capable of bypassing security scanners to deliver infostealers and conduct financial fraud. This highlights an emerging supply chain threat targeting AI-integrated platforms.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM flaw CVE-2026-20230 now exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager is under active exploitation due to a high-severity server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-20230.

articles.title: Tata Electronics confirms cyberattack as hackers leak data
articles.summary: Tata Electronics has confirmed a cyberattack on its IT infrastructure that resulted in the unauthorized exposure of company data. The incident is currently being investigated, with the company working to secure its systems.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5095093 update rolls out new Point-in-Time restore feature
articles.summary: Microsoft has released the KB5095093 preview update for Windows 11, introducing a new Point-in-Time restore feature alongside various bug fixes. This update aims to enhance system recovery capabilities for users on versions 24H2 and 25H2.

articles.title: Healthtech firm Xolis suffers data breach impacting 1.4 million people
articles.summary: Healthtech firm Xsolis confirmed a data breach affecting 1.4 million individuals resulting from a successful phishing attack on their network.

articles.title: Internet Society Foundation Opens Global Call for Common Good Cyber Fund to Strengthen Cybersecurity
articles.summary: The Internet Society Foundation has launched the Common Good Cyber Fund to provide financial support for initiatives that strengthen global cybersecurity. The project aims to improve digital resilience by funding efforts that serve the public interest.

articles.title: Five Eyes agencies sound alarm about AI’s threat to cybersecurity
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has issued a joint warning that artificial intelligence is rapidly escalating cybersecurity threats, with significant impacts expected within months rather than years.

articles.title: Justice Department seizes infrastructure used by cyber scam and criminal marketplace
articles.summary: The U.S. Justice Department has seized digital infrastructure linked to cyber scams and criminal marketplaces, while the Treasury Department sanctioned the Cambodian-based Huione Group for its involvement.

articles.summary: A new macOS campaign utilizes a 'ClickFix' technique to trick users into executing Terminal commands that silently download and launch info-stealing malware via malicious DMG files.

articles.summary: LastPass confirmed a security breach resulting from the compromise of a Klue OAuth token used by an unauthorized actor. The incident highlights a supply chain vulnerability affecting the password manager's customer data.

articles.summary: A Russian-speaking threat actor is conducting a massive credential-harvesting campaign dubbed FortiBleed, affecting over 430,000 global FortiGate firewall installations. The operation leverages brute-forcing and service exploitation to compromise systems for financial gain.

articles.summary: Security researchers at Mythos have uncovered a long-standing memory leak vulnerability dubbed 'Squidbleed' that has impacted legacy systems like NetWare, FTP, and HTTP since the late 1990s. The flaw represents a significant historical security oversight affecting archaic network protocols.

articles.title: Feds seize alleged cyber-scam infrastructure connected to Southeast Asian company
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice seized a cloud computing account linked to subsidiaries of the Huione Group, which is already sanctioned by the U.S. government for its ties to cyber-scam operations. This action represents a targeted strike against infrastructure supporting illicit financial and fraudulent activity.

articles.title: Trump directs federal agencies to protect US data from quantum threats
articles.summary: President Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to transition to post-quantum cryptography to secure sensitive data against future quantum computing capabilities.

articles.title: DifyTap: Four Bugs Put over 1 million AI Apps at Risk
articles.summary: Researchers at Zafran Labs discovered four vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws, in the open-source Dify platform that potentially expose sensitive data across over one million AI applications. These security gaps could allow unauthorized access to cross-tenant data, internal documents, and private AI conversations.

articles.title: ‘Cordyceps’ CI/CD Flaw Exposes Microsoft, Google, Apache Repos to Pipeline Hijacking
articles.summary: A CI/CD vulnerability dubbed 'Cordyceps' allows anonymous actors to exploit GitHub Actions workflows, potentially leading to build poisoning and the exposure of sensitive tokens in major projects. The flaw impacts critical infrastructure providers including Microsoft, Google, and Apache.

articles.title: The Rise of AI-Powered Academic Fraud: Beyond Traditional Plagiarism
articles.summary: The emergence of AI-generated content is transforming academic fraud by enabling the creation of original-looking work and fabricated sources, necessitating new detection capabilities for educational institutions.

articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group have entered guilty pleas for their roles in the 2024 hack of Transport for London's systems.

articles.title: Compromise kids online safety bill unveiled by House leaders, with key omission
articles.summary: House leaders have introduced a version of the kids' online safety bill that notably excludes the 'duty of care' provision designed to force platforms to mitigate algorithmic harms. This omission has drawn criticism for potentially weakening the bill's ability to protect minors from psychological and social risks online.

articles.title: Fake AI Agent Skill Passed Security Scans and Reportedly Reached 26,000 Agents
articles.summary: Security firm AIR demonstrated a significant supply chain vulnerability by successfully deploying a fake AI agent skill that bypassed all security scanners and reached 26,000 corporate and individual accounts. The experiment highlights a critical gap in the security vetting processes of popular AI agent marketplaces.

articles.summary: President Trump signed an executive order mandating that federal agencies migrate high-value systems to post-quantum cryptography by 2030 and 2031 to mitigate future quantum-computing threats. National security systems are excluded from this timeline and will follow a separate regulatory path.

articles.title: What the Fortibleed campaign means for organizations running FortiGate firewalls
articles.summary: A sophisticated, automated credential-harvesting campaign dubbed FortiBleed has compromised thousands of FortiGate firewalls by leveraging exposed attacker tools and scripts. The operation allowed attackers to gain deep access to victim networks, including full domain-level control in some instances.

articles.title: Algerian man charged with running two cybercrime marketplaces
articles.summary: An Algerian national, Abdellah Belmili, has been charged by federal prosecutors for allegedly operating two dark-web marketplaces that sold stolen financial credentials and phishing kits targeting U.S. banks.

articles.title: GitHub Updates actions/checkout to Block Common Pwn Request Attack Patterns
articles.summary: GitHub is updating the 'actions/checkout' tool to mitigate security risks associated with 'pull_request_target' triggers, which have been exploited to execute malicious code with elevated privileges. The update aims to harden software supply chain security starting June 18, 2026.

articles.title: New N-able feature gives IT teams visibility into AI usage across endpoints and networks
articles.summary: N-able has introduced a new 'Shadow AI Visibility' feature across its UEM and security platforms to help IT teams track and manage unauthorized AI tool usage on endpoints and networks. This tool aims to mitigate security risks associated with the rapid and often unmonitored adoption of AI applications within corporate environments.

articles.title: The Exploit Doesn't Exist. You Can Still Prove It Works Against You
articles.summary: The article discusses how security teams can proactively validate vulnerability exploitability to defend against threats before public exploits are released. This approach helps organizations mitigate risk despite the speed at which attackers weaponize new vulnerabilities.

articles.title: LastPass confirms data breach in Klue supply chain attack
articles.summary: LastPass confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to customer data within their Salesforce environment, resulting from a supply chain attack targeting the company's OAuth tokens via Klue.

articles.title: Dragos unveils OT-native AI to help critical infrastructure teams prioritize threats faster
articles.summary: Dragos has launched EmberAI, an operational technology-native AI tool designed to help critical infrastructure teams analyze and prioritize security threats using historical and real-time intelligence. The platform aims to improve asset visibility and vulnerability management by leveraging over a decade of specialized industrial security expertise.

articles.title: Using Reddit to manipulate AI search results is surprisingly easy
articles.summary: A Cornell Tech study reveals that AI research agents can be easily manipulated by brief, targeted Reddit comments, raising significant concerns about the integrity of AI-generated reports. This vulnerability highlights the risks of AI systems relying on unverified, community-generated content from the web.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider members plead guilty over cyberattack that crippled London transit
articles.summary: Two members of the threat group Scattered Spider have pleaded guilty to infiltrating Transport for London's network, which caused significant and long-term disruption to public transit services in 2024.

articles.title: Webinar: Why email security teams are drowning in alerts
articles.summary: The headline highlights the issue of alert fatigue in email security teams caused by the high volume of phishing and account takeover attacks. It suggests that leveraging behavioral AI for automation can improve operational efficiency and response times.

articles.title: New CryptoBandits Malware Uses USB Drives and Tor to Steal Crypto
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers have identified 'CryptoBandits,' a new malware strain that leverages USB drives and the Tor network to hijack cryptocurrency transactions by modifying wallet addresses. This dual-action clipper poses a significant risk to cryptocurrency users by redirecting funds during transfer processes.

articles.title: Agentic AI: The Weapon That No Longer Needs a Warrior
articles.summary: The rise of agentic AI represents a paradigm shift where autonomous systems can select and engage targets without direct human intervention. This evolution fundamentally alters the nature of cyber warfare by removing the human decision-maker from the loop.

articles.title: The Evolution of iGaming Fraud: What Security Teams Should Expect in 2027
articles.summary: This article explores how emerging technologies like AI, deepfakes, and fraud-as-a-service are expected to evolve the iGaming threat landscape by 2027. It provides actionable guidance for security teams to prepare their defenses against these sophisticated future risks.

articles.title: GTA 6 early access offers are taking gamers’ crypto
articles.summary: Scammers are setting up fraudulent websites promising early access to GTA 6 in exchange for cryptocurrency payments to deceive eager gamers. These sites are unauthorized and provide no access to the game, resulting in financial loss for victims.

articles.title: Xsolis Data Breach Impacts 1.4 Million People
articles.summary: Healthcare technology firm Xsolis suffered a data breach caused by a phishing attack, exposing the personal and medical information of 1.4 million individuals. The incident compromised sensitive data from the company's hospital client systems.

articles.title: 2 Scattered Spider-Linked Hackers Plead Guilty Over £39M TfL Cyberattack
articles.summary: Two teenagers associated with the Scattered Spider group have pleaded guilty to orchestrating a major cyberattack against Transport for London and various US healthcare organizations, resulting in millions of pounds of damages. The individuals are currently awaiting sentencing for their roles in the breaches.

articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider hacker group have pleaded guilty to charges linked to a 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London that incurred £29 million in costs. The defendants face sentencing in July for their violations of the UK's Computer Misuse Act.

articles.title: Omada Identity Sovereign targets Europe’s growing digital sovereignty demands
articles.summary: Omada has launched Omada Identity Sovereign to help regulated European organizations meet strict digital sovereignty and compliance requirements for identity governance. The solution is designed to align with evolving regulatory frameworks like DORA and NIS2.

articles.title: Hack The Box adds crisis simulations and SOC training to strengthen cyber readiness
articles.summary: Hack The Box has expanded its platform with new SOC training, crisis simulations, and AI-driven tools to help organizations improve cybersecurity team readiness and operational resilience. These additions aim to help security leaders identify skill gaps and better prepare for evolving AI-based cyber threats.

articles.title: Mavenir turns NOC knowledge into automation for autonomous networks
articles.summary: Mavenir has launched an Agentic Service Assurance Framework designed to automate complex network operations across 5G and cloud-native environments using a multi-agent AI system. The platform aims to streamline fault detection and resolution without requiring the replacement of existing infrastructure.

articles.title: Malicious npm Packages Pose as PostCSS Tools to Deliver Windows RAT
articles.summary: Researchers discovered malicious npm packages masquerading as PostCSS tools to infect Windows systems with a remote access trojan. The packages were recently published and have recorded several hundred downloads.

articles.title: OpenAI wants AI to fix vulnerabilities, not just find them
articles.summary: OpenAI has expanded its Daybreak initiative to integrate AI models and security tools designed to not only identify software vulnerabilities but also facilitate their automated remediation. This effort aims to alleviate industry pressure by streamlining the patching process for developers and security teams.

articles.title: F5 launches AI Security Platform to uncover and secure shadow AI
articles.summary: F5 has launched an AI Security Platform to provide visibility and governance for enterprise AI deployments, bolstered by the acquisition of SurePath AI. The platform aims to mitigate risks associated with shadow AI by continuously monitoring and protecting AI models, agents, and their connecting APIs.

articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting Microsoft 365 collaboration tools and Outlook Groups to disguise phishing attempts as routine, trusted productivity workflows. This technique bypasses traditional security filters by embedding malicious actions within legitimate-looking notifications.

articles.summary: Attackers are distributing malicious VBScript files via WhatsApp Desktop and Web to install legitimate ManageEngine RMM software, enabling unauthorized remote access. The campaign is currently targeting users across multiple global regions.

articles.title: A $1,400 experiment in AI security auditing outperformed OpenAI’s Codex Security
articles.summary: Researchers developed EVOHUNT, a system that utilizes an optimized external playbook to enable AI agents to identify software vulnerabilities more effectively than OpenAI’s commercial Codex model at a significantly lower cost. This highlights the potential for cost-effective, specialized open-source AI tools in automated security auditing.

articles.title: Five Eyes spooks warn AI means infosec incidents can become ‘major operational and financial crises’
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has warned that AI-driven cyber threats are escalating, potentially transforming routine security incidents into severe operational and financial crises. Executives are urged to prioritize robust cybersecurity measures to mitigate these emerging risks.

articles.title: OpenAI Expands Daybreak With GPT-5.5-Cyber to Help Defenders Patch Security Flaws
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched an enhanced version of its GPT-5.5-Cyber model as part of the Daybreak initiative to assist cybersecurity defenders in identifying and patching complex software vulnerabilities. This tool is designed to perform deep code analysis to help secure large codebases.

articles.title: Sniff out stale AI override advice with this open source CLI
articles.summary: A new open-source CLI tool has been released to help developers identify and remediate stale AI override advice and insecure package dependencies. The tool focuses on mitigating vulnerabilities that are often difficult to detect within software supply chains.

articles.title: OpenAI: Yoo-hoo, look over here, we do that security stuff too!
articles.summary: OpenAI has announced new security initiatives, including a 'Patch The Planet' pledge, aimed at strengthening their vulnerability management and cybersecurity posture. This move highlights the company's commitment to proactive security measures as part of their broader development strategy.

articles.title: WhatsApp phishing attack uses fake business docs to hack PCs
articles.summary: A sophisticated malware campaign is targeting WhatsApp users by sending deceptive messages containing malicious VBScript files disguised as business documents. Once executed, these files grant attackers unauthorized remote access to the victim's computer.

articles.title: JaredFromSubway MEV bot hacked in $15 million crypto theft
articles.summary: The infamous JaredFromSubway Ethereum MEV bot was exploited for $15 million after an attacker tricked its detection logic with fake trading opportunities. The incident highlights the inherent risks of automated high-frequency trading bots in the decentralized finance space.

articles.title: FFmpeg fixes PixelSmash flaw in widely used video decoder
articles.summary: The PixelSmash vulnerability in the widely used FFmpeg library allows for remote code execution and denial-of-service attacks across several popular media and cloud applications. Developers have released a fix to address the flaw and mitigate potential exploitation.

articles.title: WhatsApp Malware Campaign Hijacks Trust, Installs Legitimate Admin Tools
articles.summary: Attackers are hijacking WhatsApp accounts to distribute fake debt notices that install remote access tools, granting them unauthorized control over victims' computers. The campaign is actively ongoing and relies on the deployment of legitimate administrative software to bypass security detection.

articles.title: Cloudflare teams up with big browsers to help websites tell welcome from unwelcome visitors
articles.summary: Cloudflare has collaborated with major browser developers to implement Private Access Control Tokens, a mechanism designed to differentiate between human users and malicious bots. This initiative aims to reduce automated fraud by verifying device legitimacy without compromising user privacy.

articles.title: FortiBleed campaign used custom FortiGate sniffer to steal credentials
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign leveraged custom sniffer tools on compromised Fortinet FortiGate firewalls to harvest authentication credentials. This large-scale operation highlights a targeted effort to compromise network infrastructure to steal sensitive access data.

articles.title: Trump executive orders speed up post-quantum migration, boost industry
articles.summary: Recent executive orders signed by Donald Trump aim to accelerate the U.S. federal government's migration to post-quantum encryption while fostering the growth of the domestic quantum computing sector.

articles.title: Security shops among the 'hundreds' of Klue hack victims
